newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, fronts hold gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, fronts hold gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mixed late Monday in fairly active trade, with front months still buoyed by reports of firmer physical prices and some follow-through technical buying, market sources said.

At 1350 EDT, September was still up 7.2 cents at $2.575 per million British thermal units after hitting another new high of $2.605. October, which also set a new benchmark of $2.60 today, was 5.5 cents higher at $2.57. Others were mixed.
"It's all technical. It doesn't have much to do with the physical market except that some marketers are short this month," said one Texas-based trader.
Rising concerns about storage after three light weekly builds has been a prime driver for the recent rally, that has seen September up more than 20 percent since late July.
But many skeptics remain, citing little or no weather support this week and near-record open interest that could mean a swift slide once longs start to bail.
Temperatures in the Midwest and East this week are mostly expected to hover below seasonal levels, while the Southwest is forecast to remain hot.

Technical traders agreed the market was seriously overbought and due for a pullback. They pegged September resistance at the new contract high of $2.605, with further selling likely in the spot continuation gap between $2.64 and $2.89 from late January. Support was seen in the $2.34 area and then at $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27. Further support points were at $2.20, $2.15-2.16 and then along the short-term up trendline near $2.15.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices rebounded more than 15 cents to near the $2.50 level. Midcon pipes jumped about 20 cents to the mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas also firmed 20 cents to the low-$2.70s.
NYMEX said 39,564 contracts traded at 1300 EDT. Hub open interest on August 8 rose 6,071 contracts to 214,909, with 46,837 lots now open in September.
On the KCBT, September was still up by 4.5 cents at $2.45, while deferreds were steady to seven cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 1.2 cents to 11.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
